name: De'Medici
lede: De'Medici is a dark purplish red from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, named for the Florentine dynasty but with the exact reason undocumented in our sources.

sections.title: A dictionary name, a family nobody explains
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* (1930), as cited by NBS Circular 553 (1955), records De'Medici on plate 54, row L, column 12, first appearing in print around 1924 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system reads the swatch as "dark purplish red," its block 259 [1]. None of the 29 books in our concordance names this swatch, so whether the Medici connection is heraldic, a fashion-house reference, or a compiler's flourish is undocumented here [2].

In LCH terms it measures lightness 29, chroma 32, hue 4 degrees, Munsell 9.4RP 2.9/6.5 [1]. Its closest match in the library is [[bokhara]], about 3.1 CIEDE2000 units away, with [[velasquez]] close behind at 3.4 units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
A match within six CIEDE2000 units covering at least five percent of the canvas is rare: 15 of our 23,781 archive paintings, about 0.06 percent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 5 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.8 times the overall rate, and most often sits as a mid-tone, in 60 percent of its appearances [4].

The earliest dated match is Francisco de Osona's *Pontius Pilate Washing his Hands*, about 1500, four centuries before Maerz and Paul recorded the name in 1930; early centuries are thin in the archive, so this is a floor, not a first, and a photograph of an aged canvas is a screen color, not a pigment test [4].
